newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close higher on soybeans, China.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close higher on soybeans, China.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed higher on a technical bounce, firm soybean futures and recent demand by China for U.S. and optional origin soymeal, traders said.
"There is talk some of the China business in the soy complex last week may have been understated but there's no confirmation of that," said Mark Cermak, analyst for O'Connor and Co.
Hong Kong-based traders said China late last week bought between 120,000 and 150,000 tonnes of soymeal for November and December delivery from the U.S., South America and India.
Signals the soy complex was technically oversold after the sharp break late last week boosted prices.

The nine day relative strength (RSI) for October soymeal closed Friday at 27.84 points and October soyoil at 10.45. Technical traders generally consider an RSI of 20 or less as indicative of an oversold market.
Soyoil closed 0.10 to 0.24 cent per lb higher, with October up 0.24 at 23.56 cents. Soymeal was $2.10 per ton higher to $0.10 lower, with October up $2.10 at $246.20 a ton.
